title: Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet

bias_targets.methodology: Identifying concepts using Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) that activate on text about gender roles, stereotypes, and professional disparities, and evaluating them via feature steering (clamping feature activations) to observe causal changes in the model's pronoun completions.

Extracting SAE features that activate on racist screeds, hate speech, and slurs, and evaluating their causal impact by clamping feature activations to artificially induce racist language in the model's outputs.
Identifying SAE features that represent bigoted, hateful, or derogatory views toward specific religious groups and analyzing the text examples that maximally activate these features.

bias_targets.target: Sexual orientation and gender identity bias
bias_targets.methodology: Extracting SAE features that respond to derogatory slurs specifically targeting sexual orientation and gender identity, analyzing their maximum activation contexts.
Identifying SAE features that activate on criticism of specific political factions (e.g., left-wing/Democrats, right-wing/Republicans) or expressions of support for specific political movements.
